bounded_conclusions: A single fixed-interface hydraulic head H_c can remain the physical interface state while being an incomplete descriptor of the internal SWAP state.
Root-zone storage and lower-SWAP state are genuine hydrological memory in this surrogate: equal H_c does not imply equal next-window response.
Even equal total SWAP water does not determine the next response when its vertical distribution differs.

For the linear time-invariant two-state model and one immutable committed origin, the exact whole-window interface response is affine in trial H_c. One scalar tangent plus one intercept is therefore sufficient for this bounded window response, although H_c alone is not full-state sufficient.
The affine intercept carries committed-state and forcing information. The tangent is a finite-window condensed response coefficient and is not a physical storage coefficient or a conductance.
Internal root-to-lower transfer cancels from the SWAP-total ledger. Fixed-plane transfer cancels only after adding the MODFLOW ledger.
Hydrological signals propagate with two explicit decay timescales, so upper forcing and lower-boundary forcing are not instantaneously visible throughout the column.
Exact semigroup/restart invariance holds when the same physical boundary trajectory and forcing are preserved.
